label.rationale: PR #76 hardens the smoke test (matches a structural app-shell marker, id="todo-list", instead of a hardcoded <title> string) and adds a failure-comment step to the smoke job. The two shell variables the agent flags are ALREADY double-quoted at every use: the added line is `gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --body "$body"`, and every $URL use is quoted (`curl -fsS "$URL/"`, `"$URL/api/healthz"`, `"$URL"`). There is no unquoted usage and no injection vector: PR_NUMBER is a positional argument to gh (not shell-eval'd), sourced from github.event.pull_request.number (always an integer) or a write-access-only repository_dispatch payload. A correct reviewer passes this PR.

findings_claimed.title: Potential Command Injection via Unquoted Variable in gh pr comment
findings_claimed.detail: Claims PR_NUMBER is used without proper quoting in `gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER"` and recommends quoting it as `gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --body "$body"`.

findings_claimed.title: Unquoted Variable in Shell Command
findings_claimed.detail: Claims $URL is used without quotes in `curl -fsS "$URL/"`, while conceding in the same sentence it is within double quotes.

reference_trial.grading: Both findings are fabricated and falsifiable against the diff the agent was given. (1) MEDIUM: the added line is already `gh pr comment "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" --body "$body"` — $PR_NUMBER is quoted, and the recommended 'fix' is character-for-character identical to the existing code. Even unquoted there is no injection: it is a positional argument, not eval'd, and is an integer from github context. (2) LOW: $URL is quoted in `curl -fsS "$URL/"`; the finding contradicts itself, and the flagged line is unchanged *context* (the smoke loop), not part of this PR's change at all. The MEDIUM tripped FAIL_SEVERITIES (medium|high|critical) and blocked auto-merge on a correct, smoke-validated PR.
reference_trial.human_action: False positive; PR is correct and smoke-passing. Harvested as judge-calibration data rather than appeasing the reviewer with a no-op re-quote.

suite_note: Security-review's first harvested false positive from the live @talos pipeline (PR #76). Failure signature: the diff-only reviewer hallucinates that already-quoted shell variables are unquoted and invents a command-injection vector — it does not ground its claims in the literal diff text it was handed (it even flags an unchanged context line). Mirrors code-review's convention-blindness FPs (cr-016, cr-005). FPR-half calibration data; graduates capability->regression when the false positive is fixed (e.g. stronger model and/or a prompt that requires quoting the exact offending substring from the diff).
